entries.notes: GH #811 (Android 16, shared storage, Syncthing): pageSaves uncertain 6, toast with no step. For page saves Uncertain comes only from page_sync; a directory-sync error always names "fsync directory" and its errno, so a step-less toast was the M3-1 publication check (c69abc962). page_sync now names the case in the toast step (no stamp after rename / no file after directory sync / changed before directory sync) and the diagnostics report counts each under storage.pageSaves.uncertainProof, with which stamp fields changed and the last change's deltas (no names, paths or content). Outcomes are unchanged. The device cause is reproduced only with MediaProvider's FUSE passthrough on (ci.yml android-git-storage job 36-passthrough, run 41177645677): a replaced page's saves fail "changed before directory sync" (the replaced file's mtime lands on the new file and a passthrough read copies it into the inode after the pre-read fstat); that fix is a separate save-path change (FIX-811 r2, REG-GH811-ANDROID-PASSTHROUGH-UNCERTAIN).

entries.notes: Root cause (GH #811, FIX-811 r2): on MediaProvider FUSE a rename over a page makes the kernel flush the replaced inode's times by node id, which MediaProvider applies to the new file at that path; with persist.sys.fuse.passthrough.enable a passthrough read then copies the backing times into the inode (fuse_file_accessed). The M3-1 check compared the path after the directory sync with the publication read's handle stamp taken before its bytes, so every replacement failed and every retry replaced again. page_sync now compares with the same handle's stamp after the read (identity must match the pre-read stamp); the watcher keeps the pre-read stamp (GH #623). Cost: one handle fstat per save. A replacement during the read still fails the check; an in-place write during it is reconciled by the watcher (rev of the bytes read back). The test disturbance moves the page's mtime inside the publication read, as the passthrough read does. Device coverage: the F-M3S-1 acceptance and these tests run on shared storage in ci.yml android-git-storage, including API 36 with passthrough.

coverage.failBefore: proven: on the a399250b5 production files 33 of the 55 cases in Block.multilineExitFailure.test.tsx fail (every failed-exit, retried-exit and redo-history case for each block kind and editor; the CM6 whole-block code case fails with expected 'const x = 1' to be 'const x = 1\n'); the 22 success-path cases, which pin the undo unit and the parser and store counters measured on that base, pass on base by design. entries.notes: The multiline exit committed the trailing-blank trim to the block, then asked the kernel to insert the sibling, inside withUndoUnit. A refused or failed insert returned normally, so the unit's rollback never ran and the trim stayed. The exit is now exitMultilineBlock(id, stage(trimmed)): the kernel is asked about the insert over the trimmed text first (a PendingEdit), and the trim is written, with the insert, inside the undo unit only once it has answered. A refusal enters no unit and writes nothing, so the mounted editor keeps its node, text, caret and history. The textarea and the CodeMirror editor share the one document function.

entries.title: The git sync transport tests failed spuriously on a loaded host: the test waited at most 5 s for the fixture's held request and the fixture ended its own hold after 5 s, so a slow TLS handshake and advertisement failed the test ('fixture never received git POST') before the request it synchronizes on arrived

entries.title: An empty task (a bare TODO/DONE headline or bullet) stays a task when Tine gives it an id, folds it, schedules it or strips its id on copy, and a Logseq-written bare task with an id drawer opens as a task instead of failing to open in debug builds

coverage.failBefore: proven: see RECEIPT-fix-org-keyword-drawer.md

entries.notes: lsdoc, like mldoc 1.5.9 (oracle), accepts a bare marker only at end of input, so `* TODO` is a task and `* TODO` + `:PROPERTIES:` (or `id::`, a SCHEDULED line) is the plain word. Tine's id, fold, planning and copy-strip edits add or remove exactly those rows, so in release builds the task silently became text on the next read (bytes written were as intended); debug builds failed to open the page (I-4 assertion). Fix extends the GH741 LOGBOOK repair in lsdoc_block_parse::restore_bare_task to a title followed only by property, planning or LOGBOOK rows; body text after the title stays text. Checkpoint FORMAT 21. Divergence from Logseq's reading of the same file (Logseq shows the word): see receipt question.
